references.text: In John 9:2 the disciples ask a question about the cause of blindness (sin), while in 9:21 the parents avoid answering how the healing occurred and refer to their son.

The formerly blind man is first called in to testify about the healing, but the parents refer him to speak for himself to avoid confirming that Jesus is the prophet, just as they say he should speak on his own behalf.

The healed man later confirms that he knows he was blind and now sees, and that he does not know if Jesus is a sinner, which directly responds to the parents' statement that they do not know how he sees or who opened his eyes.
The Pharisees cast out the healed man, showing the consequence of confessing faith in Jesus, in contrast to the parents' fear of excommunication that led them to refer to their son.
Many believed in Jesus but did not confess it publicly because they feared the Pharisees and excommunication, just as the parents in chapter 9 avoid confirming the healing.
